Loved the Humankind Revolution, but this is rather a pass for me in 2026. Maybe it's just too old by this point. Prague looks cool (although not as cool as gold filter in the original), however the gameplay feels just old and still unpolished. Some small bugs, inconsistent stealth, movable objects vibrate and bug out, shooting is just crap.... Something screams the game is incomplete both mechanically and story-wise.

This game is pretty fun. Many levels and obstacles can be solved in different ways or using different augmentations.

The ending is a bit abrupt; I heard the studio ran out of funding for the game. Overall, I'm still satisfied with the ending and game.

Wow, I refused to buy this game for so long because of the critics saying that this game ends up halfway through the story, but that is so not true, sure the way it ends clearly shows that there is more to it, and that a sequel will happen (hopefuly), but nonetheless, it also brings closure to the main plot of this episode... that is the main source of its bad critics, that and the DX12 glitches, while the latter remains true to this day -but the are minor annoyances easily solable by a save/reload)- the former has been so unfair, it is forgetting how the 2 first titles were

The game is beautifuly executed, the gunfights are tough : you are not a terminator, at least through the first playthrough, ond much like deus ex the second (and the first ? don't remember), side quests shows up in the ending, even though we don't see much of their consequences on the world. Very nice level (and art) design, multiple ways of doing things

Well, I won't repeat more what has already been said numerous times (pros and cons) everywhere else.

ANNOYING UNSKIPPABLE CREDITS THOUGH

This game is great, IF you're returning to it for the nostalgia. The PC port wasn't very optimized, and in order to run the game smoothly, i had to set every setting one lower and turn the resolution to 1440x900. I went to fire it up [the day this is written] after playing the night before with no problems,and its stuttering, frames are lagging, input registration is lagging, input is lagging, and its things like this as to why I can't recommend this to others. When it decides to work right, it looks great, feels great, but its the initial getting it to work that I think really hurts this game for new players. If you're okay with pushing through it, its a great game to play, the story is great, the choices are seemingly endless, hell I've found ways to path playing it again now, that I never knew about when I played on console.

All in all, I would not recommend to new players. Returning fans are sure to have a blast.
fuck elon musk, this game and overall series (books included) goes against everything he believes in, yet he claims to love it.

This is a quality sequel that refines upon everything that made Human Revolution great.

Unfortunately it seems like it was a victim of development crunch. If you have played Human Revolution, you are accustomed to exploring and investigating an area with the chapter culminating in a boss fight. If you made the mistake of playing this one directly after, you will spend about 20 hours exploring the first city while looking forward to a boss fight and the next chapter. Except there is no next chapter. There is one boss, and the game ends. While this game has much more detail, Human Revolution covered much more ground.

I'd recommend it if you can treat it as supplement to Human Revolution. As its own game, it is claustrophobic and short.
It resolves none of the cliffhangers of HR, and adds little to the story other than depicting the sociopolitical aftermath of HR.

Grab it on sale

Great game.
I avoided this game for a long time due to the "mixed reception", but that was stupid on my part.
I would say that in the series Mankind Divided is second only to the original Deus Ex (haven't played Invisible war though).

The atmosphere and setting are great, the world feels believable and not forced. The division between augmented and non-augmented people is being brought up constantly and is not just a throwaway line There's some globetrotting, but mainly the game is set in Prague.

You can solve certain quests "in advance" and also think outside the box sometimes. Exploring Prague is fun, and the game rewards you for it.

The game still looks pretty beautiful and offers some amazing visuals that stay with you. For example the London skyline was something that made me stop advancing for a while just to admire the view.

The main story is probably the least interesting thing. I couldn't tell you what the story is about if you asked me. The world and, the places and side quests were much more interesting. There's also many augmentations and enough customizable weapons to encourage different kind of play styles.

I liked Human revolution, but this one made me want to begin a new game almost immediately after finishing it just to see how differently things could be done. Highly recommended.
Almost a decade later, this game still looks as beautiful as ever. A classic fans can comeback to and enjoy.

Huge fan of Deus Ex Universe! Loved HR and MD is a great sequel after that (though HR is the superior one), lots of update in game mechanism! 27 hour played so far but only did prologue and 5 side missions! :D
I'm drinking every last drop of this one! Give me more Deus Ex!!

Bought this game on sale recently,

Was a fan of the first game but held off buying this 2nd installment for a long time due to the reviewers saying this game was plagued with microtransactions

I enjoyed this game A LOT! The story pacing was good and kept you on the edge the entire time. The ending left some loose ends and was a cliffhanger by design; but that just leaves me wanting for more. Gameplay is superb and arguably the best part of the game. The stealth mechanics reward creativity and patience, while combat rewards strategy and planning as well as good aim. Level designs are magnificent, I can only imagine the work that was put into making the settings. REal amazing.

On the downside, the DLCs are disappointing. Character progression does not carry over and its tedious to play simply because they are side stories that do not compliment or enhance the main plot.

OVerall I think its a very worth it purchase. I should've bought this when it first came out, unfortunately i let the negative reviews cloud my perception.

Fun game with a long enough story to keep you hooked throughout the game. Also a lot of cool abilities and choices you get to make as the player that can change how the whole game will play out, making the replay value higher if you really enjoyed your first playthrough.

Such a great immersive-sim. I preferred non-lethal stealth gameplay and I absolutely liked it. I literally was checking every single nook for resources/easter eggs because locations in this game are perfect, because I’ve never played a game where I play in Prague, so it is kind of unique for me. Also this game has good skill tree, would not say it is revolutionary, but just solid, so it allows you to build Adam like you want.

11/10

Hikaye ve karakter anlamında malesef ilkine göre daha vasat. Oyunun sonuna doğru sırf bitsin diye oynuyorsunuz. Grafikler senesinde göre güzel ancak bende mi oldu bilemem arada sapıtıyordu. Ama nolursa olsun bir Deus Ex oynuyorum diyorsunuz. O çeşitliliği size sunuyor oyun. (ister herkesi öldür, istersen kimseye duyurmadan sadece hedefini) 3-5 tane yeni experimental augmentation koymuşlar onları da oyunun ortasında anca adam akıllı kullanabiliyoruz. Olmaz ki böyle.

Not sure why I played this game for so long years ago ... because when I picked it up again I did not get into it again.
From unskipable waffle fests, terrible controls and mechanics and unclear mission statements

Another solid addition to the Deus Ex universe. A couple of bugs and some things that I didn't love, but overall it's a solid RPG with great storytelling, stealth, multiple ways to tackle situations, and fun combat.

After 33 hours, I ran into a bug that apparently is, and has been, frequent for the past 7-8 years. The bug in question? Being unable to save your game. I tried all the single fixes I could see that was viable, and nothing worked. That leaves me stuck 33 hours in, unable to progress the game unless I just play the game to the end without dying.

Or I can just uninstall the game and recommend others to steer clear from this game. The gameplay was enjoyable, the story was fairly uninspiring (but not necessarily bad), and had the game continued the way it would have towards the end, it would have been a solid 7.5 or 8 out of 10. 

A gamebreaking bug, unfixed for almost a decade by a high end developer and publisher? Now that is an immediate 1/10 from me.
I've never played Deus Ex before, read or whatever, bought this for a really good price on sale. Now, I'm gonna get all the others because this one was simply amazing.
love this game, detailed world space, good exploration, story is good hope they come back to this franchise
I think Embracer Group had a valuable asset in their hands and they let him slipped away. He could have been very useful in the coming storm. We never ask for this!

I simply love this game and its climate. Finished it 3 times already thanks to its replayability and enormous fun it gives.
Please devs, just make the next part of Adam's story - insta buy!
Hacking puzzle sucks. Even sometime the level 1 puzzle play like level 5 puzzle, like how fast you are detected. Everything else ok.

Alright. Played the game on Linux, RTX 2070 Super, and overall experience was great except one thing...

Constant memory leaks! Throughout all game constant crashes because of out-of-memory daemon killing the game, which ate all the RAM!!! I have about 13GB free ram for game and yet this is not enough!

For comparison I played The Witcher 3 GOTY Edition without single crash, except probably one hang (single. hang. in. entire. walkthrough). But no crash! Memory was enough to run youtube podcasts and stuff alongside.

But in Deus Ex crashes forced me to to even throw away my goal to run game without being spotted just so I finish it and suffering stops.

About the gameplay and plot. Gameplay has improved significantly, the plot however... I mean an idea of DE:HR is still intact. the Illuminati, the conspiracy it's all over the place here too. but Jensen himself isn't as motivated as he used to be. Deus Ex was about Jensen making his way through all the obstacles for his waifu, now it's about him unravelling secrets. For justice? Maybe. For closure? Maybe. For finding new sense of life? Maybe. But the game doesn't focus on any of the thing listed thus making his motivations unclear, unfocused, blurred.

Still, I recommend it

Abilities and maps allow you to go through this game either with brutal force or like a ghost; there's also so much replay value on top of the already fantastic game. What a game, what an experience!

It was a nice game until first boss fight and cutscene, where further plan of action was discussed. I thought that it is beginning of chapter 2, but it turns out to be the end of the game. Chapter 2 and 3 are missing. I do not recommend this game because we barely scratch conspiracy plans by the end of the game. And half of the side quests are also without proper ending.
One more huge drawback is that there is only one relative small location with free travel, Prague. At least one more city is absolutely necessary.

Good, but just not as great as Human Revolution (HR). Story was acceptable, nothing groundbreaking. Gameplay is largely the same as HR. Graphics are an improvement from HR but personally that doesn't mean much to me. If you loved HR then give this a go, otherwise get it at a reduced price.

The first is to have an abrupt, unceremonious ending with no closure and the second is

Deus Ex: Mankind Divided is better than Cyberpunk 2077.

Why?
Because it's narrative is better paced.
Because it's darker.
Because the world feels less comical.
Because the themes feel real and as if they can become a reality in the near futury.

It's a shame we never got a sequel. Adam Jensen is one of the coolest characters in recent video game history.
I'd love to see him in another game some day.

I own the official Mankind Divided trenchcoat Musterbrand produced back then and I still wear it to this day.

Yes, I love Deus Ex.

First off I want to clarify that I know Deus Ex's budget was alot smaller than Project Red's and it was released 5-8 years prior to Cyberpunk but that game Is where I came from and I loved it.

I'm not sure what to think about this one.
I was so overwhelmed by CP2077 and was really excited to try Dues Ex.
However Deus Ex feels like everything I liked about the Cyberpunk: The world, the feel and the story was just unsatisfying and felt off in my opinion. I don't want to list everything I did not like in my first hour because I think it does not deserve this negative feedback. I just did not enjoy the timeI had with it and I don't think I will pick it up again any time soon.

In my opinion Cyberpunk2077 in 2024 still has it's own flaws and missed opportunities but I think it plays in an entirely different league. One Think I like about Deus Ex though is it's worlddesign. It feels like it plays in between Our reality today and Cyberpunk2077s society and stage of technical development. It feels like a proper predecessor.

yes the criticism for this game is true, the game is short, sorta feels incomplete and brings more questions than answers in the deus ex IP.
however it's still a deus ex game and these just sorta hook you in, very immersive, and this entry benefits from a nice modernization of the gameplay that was definitely needed in the series.

Some games have a vast, open world to explore. This is not one of them.
Some games have over 30 hours of gameplay. This is not one of them.

This game you will play for the music and the atmosphere. And I promise you, it will be enough.

The best moment in this game was killing all cops in one district using hacked turrets and robots and after that robbing a whole bank with noone inside but turrets and robots, which I could hack again. Wait until the shit hits the fan then spin it!

Otherwise I think the Human Revolution was probably better. Maybe it is justbe cause now it was not that unique to me... Anyway not a bad game at all.

Performancewise - i8600k @4.1 + GTX1070 and 16GB RAM -> 1080p mostly above 60 on ultra with no MSAA. Pretty GPU demanding, CPU was cool.

I'm of the same mindset as others, when I wish there were a point between recommend and not recommend. Overall, I enjoyed Human Revolution a whole lot more. The story felt more developed, the levels were more memorable, and there were a lot more weapon varieties. (no laser gun? no plasma rifle?) A lot of the "special" guns found in Mankind Divided are completely worthless. A high rate-of-fire machine gun that only shoots EMP rounds? What's the point? A cool, high-ammo capacity shotgun that only shoots hard to find armor piercing rounds? Again, why?

And the complaints of the game ending too fast are completely accurate. This really feels like a cash grab and an attempt to make money off of their previous achievement rather than an honest attempt to make the best game that they can. It does give you the feeling that they're intending to slowly release the rest of the game through DLC that will bloat the price up over $90. And it's a shame, too, because there are so many things that are good about this game. If you can get it at half off, then go for it, it's worth that. But if I were rating it, I'd give it a 6/10, maybe a 6.5/10. Not worth the full price, and kind of a lazy effort by the developer. They did "just good enough".

Eidos Montreal's unfinished masterpiece.

Sure the main story is underwhelming, the game ends out of nowhere and it's obvious Square Enix chopped the game in half to sell MTX you don't even need to buy, but if you look past all these flaws, this game is a shinning testament to smaller is better level design.

You can explore every single building is Prague, with it own little story and conspiracy. This game is best played taking your time, exploring the hub world and treating this as an environmental storytelling driven RPG first, and a stealth shooter second.

I highly recommend playing with objective markers turn off and your brain turned on (as it should be when playing any Imsim).

I rate this a 5/10 (Mankind Divided can get the other 5/10 when whoever owns them finally lets them make the sequel to this unfinished game).

The story and characters aren't as good as Human Revolution, but that isn't to say that it's not close or that gameplay isn't solid. If you manage to get the DLCs cheap, you're in for a swell ride. In short, if you liked previous games of the series you'll enjoy this one.

This game is good, but it's hardly polished in the stability section.
I have a Ryzen 7 2700x 8 cores 16 threads, and a GTX1080 OC edition 32Gbs DDR4 3600mhz RAM and I cant play this game without it crashing. Dont play this game until they fix DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED

The story is a bit of a stump but the environmental design and the tremendous amount of detail in the game areas is something I haven't seen in any other game.

Pros
+Superb level design
+Nice Deus Ex lore
+Convincing dystopian atmosphere thanks to the appropriate ambient soundtracks
+Very decent FPS mechanics; guns feel powerful and realistic

Cons
-Underwhelming story, especially towards the end
-Game enforces pacifist playstyle too much

This game is a step backwards from Human Revolution, but still a fun game. The combat and stealth system is good and the graphics are great. But the story is just not well written. If you liked Human Revolution you will probably enjoy this game, but you'll probably find the story to be a solid C+.

Okay, so.. the game in itself is awesome! The world is beautiful, the story is great, the "open-worldedness" is fantastic, the side missions are also cool! It's great that every single goal can be achieved in multiple different ways. I must say though, I'm not the most objective person when it comes to cyberpunk anything, as I love this genre.

What I didn't like:
- The game kept crashing randomly until I disabled dx12. After that, all was fine.
- The enemies are a bit dumb. :)
- The end credits. Those credits... it took 20 minutes of my life. 20 minutes! Why?! There was no clear way of skipping it either. Sure, the internet must know how, but there should be a prompt somewhere saying [Press Space] t skip Credits or something. 20 minutes, man!

Worth it for $10 USD. Don't bother with the DLC because you'll be bored of the game and the only good one is the post-game Prison.

The game as a whole is nowhere near as good as Human Revolution. The characters are shallower, there are less locations to explored, the storyline is boring and ultimately doesn't satisify the major questions raised during the game.

I expect that the publisher & developers were intended to use them as a sequal hook for the final part of a triology but it's never going to come now that the dev has been hacked apart to work on mobile games.

It's such a sad end to what both the original Deus Ex and the reboot Human Revolution built.

I give it a 6.5/10. I also had major technical troubles, having to disable SLI. The performance was also abysmal. It'll last about 20 to 30 hours but it won't be a game you want to play again or be that enthralled with while doing it.

Well. After you get past the first mission, which is kinda weak to be fair, it really opens up. It's almost more "Deus Ex" than Deus Ex. Brilliant level design, musical score off the chart. Shouldn't really expect anything less from Eidos Montreal.

Plenty of nods to the original (I'm talking about the old old Deus Ex) and I really feel they did a better job than Human revolutions.

If this is on sale then wtf are you waiting for?

Alright, I just finished the whole game with all side missions, POIs etc. on normal so here are my thoughts.

In my 18 hours of playtime I've had to forcefully shut down the game 3 times. Two when my game refused to load, and once because of a freeze.

I liked the atmosphere, talking to people, and immersing myself.

I thought the gunplay and stealth was passable. Both were functional, but not too deep.

Remote hacking is cool.

I thought the story and game was too short / simplistic.

I don't think it's worth full price, however the game goes on sale often enough.

In the end I do not regret playing it.

maybe the game optimisation is a bit trash and maybe the story is not deep as the last one but the game play if fucking epic man the whole game is just very well made it's really hard challenging game and this is not a shooter game it's more like hitman and dishonored style of games or let's say it has its own game style. I really love it and I really like it. I totally recommend it

Great game ruined by negligence. Lost 6 straight hours of progress to the savegame bug. Half a year and this critical issue has not been fixed? Only realized too late when game stopped creating new saves. Even unable to load autosaves. There appear to be user found workarounds, but having customers jump through hoops to make up for the maker's incompetence is NOT an acceptable solution.

I absolutely cannot recommend buying this game until the bug is officially fixed. This is a problem that ANY player will be bound to encounter. It is an agonizing experience to lose time and effort. A massive turn off from wanting to play again. Could they not code the game to detect failure to save on the Steam cloud, and automatically fall back to saving on the local drive? Even a simple fix like that could not be made in half a year? Negligent AND incompetent!

An amazing continuation of an amazing series. Sadly it hasn't finished the story but it was great nontheless.
The formula of the series has been further improved and although no that much has been changed compared to Human Revolution, I don't think that's a bad thing.
Just like before there are things to do everywhere and exploration and multitude of ways to do things are both fantastic as they used to be.

It's been a decade since a proper AAA immersive sim has dropped. Deathloop's setting was so weak, on that f*ck*as* island. The people yearn for cyberpunk cityscapes. I promise you'll make money. And if you don't you'll have made me happy, which is just as good if not better.

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (75%): players praise the story and characters most, but they also complain about them more than anything else.
Gameplay and combat earn praise, while bugs and crashes are a frequent complaint.

details.text: Recent reviews are more positive, at 84%, than the all-time score.
Newer players are far less positive than long-time players, at 29% against 90%.
